newsitem.title: FRANCE: French state fined for doctor's HIV.
newsitem.headline: French state fined for doctor's HIV.

text.p: The French state was ordered on Wednesday to pay 5.5 million francs ($922,000) damages to a surgeon who became HIV positive when he cut himself while operating on a patient suffering from AIDS, radio France-Info said.
Dr Patrick Cohen was employed by a state hospital outside Paris when the incident occurred in 1983.
A woman on whom he subsequently operated, before knowing about his own condition, also became HIV positive, the radio said.
The condition of Cohen and that of the woman were stable, the radio said.

Cohen told French media he believed the incident would not have occurred if he had been equipped with special gloves which he said government hospitals still mostly lacked because of their high cost and a repeat of the incident was possible.
The court in Versailles, near Paris, also sentenced the state to pay 150,000 francs ($25,000) to each of Cohen's four children in damages, the radio said.
Human Immuodeficiency Virus or HIV causes Acquired Immune Deficiency or AIDS.
